terms.comment: Our choice: no reference work has a word for a swipe. A swipe is a sweep of the finger across the glass, and verrere, to sweep, says so at once: digitō verre. Lewis & Short gives the perfect verrī from the grammarians and notes that neither perfect was in use; the present system is all one needs. Left and right: ad laevam, ad dextram.
Traupman’s verb for dragging with the mouse; it suits a slow drag better than a quick swipe.

phrases.latin: Digitō verre, et aliam imāginem vidēbis.
phrases.english: Swipe and you’ll see another picture.

sources: Lewis & Short: verro · Lewis & Short: traho
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 260.
